propositions: A check whose pass result or absence result is indistinguishable from the check never running cannot be reliably trusted to detect the condition it verifies

Absence assertions on subprocess/file/network output without producer-liveness verification (exit status, non-empty capture, or explicit presence check) fail open and pass both when the condition is met and when the producer crashes or emits nothing
Grep/regex patterns over tool output without established producer-liveness checks produce false definite verdicts when the tool never ran, was killed, or produced zero output

Silent lookup misses, unchecked return codes, pgrep patterns that self-match, and any best-effort check whose failure is invisible create the same false-confidence problem in shipped code as in test oracles
The fail-open defect has a mirror: a broken instrument can produce a confident failing result for a reason other than the condition, leading to false alarms and unnecessary recovery actions
Producer-liveness language must be added to existing tests and error-handling criteria to detect both passing and failing definite results that cannot be distinguished from instrument failure
